# Model and source

Liu et al. (2023) analysed the second-line non-small cell lung cancer (2L NSCLC)
expansion cohort of the phase I trial of bintrafusp alfa (NCT02517398), a
bifunctional fusion protein that blocks PD-L1 and traps TGF-beta. Eighty patients
were randomized 1:1 to 500 or 1200 mg every 2 weeks (q2w). The paper builds three
models, all shipped here:

* `Liu_2023_bintrafuspAlfa` -- two-compartment population PK model (Appendix S1,
  Supplementary Table S2).
* `Liu_2023_bintrafuspAlfa_tgi` -- tumour growth inhibition (TGI) model of the sum of
  longest diameters (SLD) of target lesions (Appendix S1, Supplementary Table S2).
* `Liu_2023_bintrafuspAlfa_multistate` and `Liu_2023_bintrafuspAlfa_multistate_dose` --
  the six-state multistate model of tumour response, progression and survival, in
  its final (dose-independent) form and in the dose-dependent form the authors used
  for their dose-response simulations (Table 2).

Neither the PK model nor the TGI model feeds the multistate model: individual
clearance, dose and tumour-dynamic metrics were screened as predictors of the
transitions but none was retained.

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Liu_2023_bintrafuspAlfa_multistate"))$reference`
* Article (open access): <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12976>
* PMC record with Appendices S1-S2, Supplementary Figures S1-S6 and Tables S1-S5:
  <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC10681430/>

# Population

The 80 patients (40 per arm) had advanced NSCLC after failure of first-line
therapy; mean age 63.9 and 62.1 years (range 38-85), mean body weight 68.0 and
70.8 kg, 29% women overall (40% vs 18% by arm), 49% White and 50% Asian (Asian
patients came from Korean and Taiwanese sites), all ECOG 0-1, 81% with metastases
at baseline (Liu 2023 Table 1). Tumour assessments per RECIST 1.1 by independent
review were scheduled every 6 weeks in the first year and every 12 weeks
thereafter. The multistate data held 406 observations (75 SD, 127 PR, 124 PD and
80 absorbing events: 56 deaths, 13 dropouts, 11 censored at data cutoff).

The same information is available programmatically through each model's
`population` metadata, e.g.
`readModelDb("Liu_2023_bintrafuspAlfa_multistate")()$population`.

# Population PK model

## Simulation

Both arms receive six 1-hour infusions every 2 weeks. The infusion duration
follows from Supplementary Table S1 and Figure S2, where the end-of-infusion
samples are the samples taken 1 hour after the start of the dose.

```{r pk-cohort}
mod_pk <- readModelDb("Liu_2023_bintrafuspAlfa")
n_per_arm <- 200
tau <- 336 # h, every 2 weeks
obs_rel <- c(0, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 24, 48, 96, 168, 240, 336)

make_pk_cohort <- function(n, dose, id_offset) {
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n)
  dosing <- expand.grid(id = ids, k = 0:5) |>
    mutate(time = k * tau, evid = 1L, amt = dose, rate = dose / 1, cmt = "central") |>
    select(-k)
  obs <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = unique(c(obs_rel, 5 * tau + obs_rel))) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, rate = 0, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(dosing, obs) |>
    mutate(treatment = paste(dose, "mg q2w")) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}
events_pk <- bind_rows(
  make_pk_cohort(n_per_arm, 500, 0L),
  make_pk_cohort(n_per_arm, 1200, n_per_arm)
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(events_pk[events_pk$evid == 0, c("id", "time")]))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20231)
sim_pk <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_pk, events = events_pk, keep = "treatment", returnType = "data.frame")
```

```{r pk-figure, fig.cap = "Simulated bintrafusp alfa concentrations after the first and sixth dose (median and 5th-95th percentiles, 200 virtual patients per arm). Compare with Supplementary Figures S1 and S4 of Liu 2023."}
sim_pk |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  group_by(treatment, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = median(Cc), Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 168, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~treatment) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after first dose (weeks)", y = "Bintrafusp alfa (ug/mL)")
```

## PKNCA

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- sim_pk |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
nca_dose <- events_pk |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 5 * tau),
  end = c(tau, 6 * tau),
  cmax = TRUE,
  tmax = TRUE,
  clast.obs = TRUE,
  auclast = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = intervals
))
nca_tab <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "clast.obs", "auclast")) |>
  mutate(Dose = ifelse(start == 0, "First dose", "Sixth dose")) |>
  group_by(treatment, Dose, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = signif(median(PPORRES), 3), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median)
nca_tab |>
  rename(
    "Arm" = treatment,
    "Cmax (ug/mL)" = cmax,
    "C at 336 h, trough (ug/mL)" = clast.obs,
    "AUC0-336 h (h*ug/mL)" = auclast
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Median simulated NCA parameters over the first and sixth dosing intervals.")
```

Liu 2023 reports no NCA table, so the check is structural. At steady state the
typical-value AUC over one dosing interval must equal Dose / CL, and the PK is
dose-proportional (Results: 'dose-proportional PKs and close to complete
separation of systemic exposures between the two dose groups').

```{r pk-check}
# Typical values: omega zeroed, so the note about a multi-subject solve
# without omega is expected.
typ <- suppressWarnings(rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_pk, "omega"),
  events = events_pk |> filter(id %in% c(1, n_per_arm + 1)),
  keep = "treatment", returnType = "data.frame"
), classes = "warning")
typ_nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(typ |> select(id, time, Cc, treatment), Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(events_pk |> filter(evid == 1, id %in% c(1, n_per_arm + 1)) |> select(id, time, amt, treatment), amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 5 * tau, end = 6 * tau, auclast = TRUE)
))
auc_ss <- as.data.frame(typ_nca) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  mutate(dose = ifelse(treatment == "500 mg q2w", 500, 1200), expected = dose / 0.0143,
         pct_diff = 100 * (PPORRES / expected - 1))
knitr::kable(auc_ss |> select(treatment, PPORRES, expected, pct_diff) |>
  rename("Arm" = treatment, "Typical AUCtau,ss (h*ug/mL)" = PPORRES, "Dose / CL" = expected, "% difference" = pct_diff),
  digits = 2)
# Trapezoidal AUC over a 12-point interval grid, after 9 terminal half-lives:
# a mis-transcribed CL or a unit slip moves this by far more than 3%.
stopifnot(all(abs(auc_ss$pct_diff) < 3))
```

# Tumour growth inhibition model

The TGI time axis starts at the screening scan, where the baseline SLD (IBASE) is
estimated; drug-induced shrinkage starts at the first dose, `T_SCAN_TO_DOSE`
later. The cohort uses the mean screening-to-first-dose interval of 17.6 days
(2.51 weeks) for every patient.

```{r tgi-sim}
mod_tgi <- readModelDb("Liu_2023_bintrafuspAlfa_tgi")
t_scan <- 17.6 / 7
tgi_times <- seq(0, 60, by = 0.5)
events_tgi <- expand.grid(id = 1:200, time = tgi_times) |>
  mutate(evid = 0L, cmt = "tumor_size", T_SCAN_TO_DOSE = t_scan) |>
  arrange(id, time)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20232)
sim_tgi <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_tgi, events = events_tgi, returnType = "data.frame")
```

```{r tgi-figure, fig.cap = "Simulated SLD of target lesions versus time after the first dose (median and 5th-95th percentiles of the individual predictions, 200 virtual patients). Compare with Supplementary Figure S5 of Liu 2023, whose observed median is about 58 mm before treatment, rises to about 63 mm at week 6 and settles near 40 mm from week 30."}
sim_tgi |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(tumor_size, 0.05), Q50 = median(tumor_size), Q95 = quantile(tumor_size, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time - t_scan, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
  labs(x = "Time after first dose (weeks)", y = "Sum of longest diameters (mm)")
```

The observed medians of Figure S5 come from patients still on study, and
patients who progress drop out of the tumour-size data, so the simulated median
(which keeps every patient) need not follow the late observed median.

The typical-value trajectory has a closed form. Before the first dose the SLD
grows linearly, `IBASE + KG t`; afterwards, with `A(T) = (kD / lambda)(1 - exp(-lambda T))`,
`SLD(T) = exp(-A(T)) [SLD(T0) + KG * integral_0^T exp(A(u)) du]`.

```{r tgi-check}
typ_tgi <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_tgi, "omega"), events = events_tgi |> filter(id == 1), returnType = "data.frame")
kg <- 1.43; kd <- 0.0306; lam <- 0.00559; ibase <- 56.3
A <- function(T) kd / lam * (1 - exp(-lam * T))
closed <- vapply(typ_tgi$time, function(tt) {
  if (tt <= t_scan) return(ibase + kg * tt)
  T <- tt - t_scan
  exp(-A(T)) * (ibase + kg * t_scan + kg * integrate(function(u) exp(A(u)), 0, T)$value)
}, numeric(1))
rel_err <- abs(typ_tgi$tumor_size / closed - 1)
c(max_rel_err = max(rel_err), nadir_mm = min(closed[typ_tgi$time > t_scan]),
  nadir_week_after_dose = typ_tgi$time[which.min(ifelse(typ_tgi$time > t_scan, closed, Inf))] - t_scan)
# Same parameters on both sides: the difference is LSODA tolerance only.
stopifnot(max(rel_err) < 1e-4)
```

# Multistate model

All patients start in stable disease (S1) at the first dose. Transitions are
forward only: S1 to response (S2), progression (S3), unknown (S4), dropout (S5) or
death (S6); S2 to S3, S4 or S6; S3 to S5 or S6; S4 to S5 or S6. Each ODE state is
the probability of occupying that state, so a solve without any data returns the
marginal state-occupancy curves of a patient population. When fitting, the
source resets all states after each observation to the observed state; the
shipped model reproduces that with `evid = 5` replace events.

The models have no between-subject variability, so the validation below is
deterministic. Each arm is a mixture of patients with and without baseline
metastases in the Table 1 proportions (33 of 40 at 500 mg, 32 of 40 at 1200 mg);
age only moves the very small background mortality and is set to the arm mean.

```{r ms-setup}
mod_ms <- readModelDb("Liu_2023_bintrafuspAlfa_multistate")
mod_msd <- readModelDb("Liu_2023_bintrafuspAlfa_multistate_dose")
weeks_per_month <- 365.25 / 12 / 7
ms_times <- seq(0, 180, by = 0.25)
grid <- tibble(
  id = 1:4,
  arm = rep(c("500 mg q2w", "1200 mg q2w"), each = 2),
  DOSE_HIGH = rep(c(0, 1), each = 2),
  MET_GE1 = rep(c(0, 1), 2),
  AGE = rep(c(63.9, 62.1), each = 2),
  w = c(7 / 40, 33 / 40, 8 / 40, 32 / 40)
)
events_ms <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = grid$id, time = ms_times) |>
  left_join(grid |> select(id, DOSE_HIGH, MET_GE1, AGE), by = "id") |>
  mutate(evid = 0L, cmt = "s_stable")

# The multistate models have no between-subject variability by design, so
# rxSolve's note about a multi-subject solve without omega is expected.
solve_ms <- function(mod, params = NULL) {
  suppressWarnings(
    rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events_ms, params = params, returnType = "data.frame"),
    classes = "warning"
  ) |>
    left_join(grid |> select(id, arm, w), by = "id")
}
arm_mix <- function(d, value) {
  d |>
    mutate(v = {{ value }}) |>
    group_by(arm, time) |>
    summarise(v = sum(w * v), .groups = "drop")
}
```

The ODE system is checked against its one closed-form piece: S1 is left only by
constant hazards and the Weibull k13, so
`P1(t) = exp(-(k12 + k14 + k15 + k16) t - (scale13 t)^shape13 exp(beta (1 - MET_GE1)))`.

```{r ms-check}
ms_dose <- solve_ms(mod_msd)
p1 <- ms_dose |>
  mutate(closed = exp(-(k12 + k14 + k15 + k16) * time -
    (scale13 * time)^shape13 * exp(-1.430 * (1 - MET_GE1))))
c(max_rel_err_P1 = max(abs(p1$prob_stable_disease / p1$closed - 1)),
  max_mass_balance_err = max(abs(ms_dose$prob_state_sum - 1)))
stopifnot(
  max(abs(p1$prob_stable_disease / p1$closed - 1)) < 1e-3,
  max(abs(ms_dose$prob_state_sum - 1)) < 1e-6
)
```

## State occupancy (Figure 2)

```{r ms-figure2, fig.cap = "Probability of occupying each state by dose arm (dose-dependent model). Compare with the state-proportion panels of Figure 2 of Liu 2023."}
state_labels <- c(
  prob_stable_disease = "Stable disease", prob_tumor_response = "Response",
  prob_progressive_disease = "Progression", prob_unknown_status = "Unknown",
  prob_dropout = "Dropout", prob_death = "Death"
)
ms_dose |>
  select(id, time, arm, w, all_of(names(state_labels))) |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(names(state_labels)), names_to = "state", values_to = "p") |>
  group_by(arm, state, time) |>
  summarise(p = sum(w * p), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(state = factor(state_labels[state], levels = state_labels)) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, p, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~state, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time after first dose (weeks)", y = "Probability", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## PFS, OS and response by dose (Figure 3)

The end points follow the paper's definitions (Methods, 'Derivation of PFS and
OS'):

* **PFS**: progression is only seen at a tumour assessment (every 6 weeks in year
  one, every 12 weeks after), while death from S1/S2 counts when it happens;
  transitions to unknown or dropout censor PFS. Under the model's Markov
  assumption, censoring that is independent of the hazards leaves the
  event-free curve of a world without those transitions, so PFS at an assessment
  is `P1 + P2` from a solve with k14, k24 and the dropout hazard switched off.
* **OS**: time to dropout or death, `1 - P5 - P6`.
* **Overall response rate**: the probability of ever entering the response state,
  `integral of k12 * P1 dt`, up to 180 weeks of follow-up.

```{r ms-endpoints}
off <- log(1e-12)
ms_pfs <- solve_ms(mod_msd, params = c(
  lk14_500mg = off, lk14_1200mg = off, lk24_500mg = off, lk24_1200mg = off,
  lkdrop_500mg = off, lkdrop_1200mg = off
))
visits <- c(seq(6, 48, by = 6), seq(60, 180, by = 12))
pfs <- arm_mix(ms_pfs, prob_stable_disease + prob_tumor_response) |>
  filter(time %in% visits)
os <- arm_mix(ms_dose, 1 - prob_dropout - prob_death)
orr <- ms_dose |>
  group_by(id, arm, w) |>
  arrange(time, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  summarise(orr = sum(diff(time) * (head(k12 * prob_stable_disease, -1) + tail(k12 * prob_stable_disease, -1)) / 2),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(orr = sum(w * orr))

pfs_step <- bind_rows(
  tibble(arm = unique(pfs$arm), time = 0, v = 1),
  pfs
)
bind_rows(
  pfs_step |> mutate(endpoint = "PFS"),
  os |> mutate(endpoint = "OS")
) |>
  filter(time <= 150) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, 100 * v, colour = arm)) +
  geom_step(data = ~ filter(.x, endpoint == "PFS")) +
  geom_line(data = ~ filter(.x, endpoint == "OS")) +
  facet_wrap(~endpoint) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("500 mg q2w" = "red", "1200 mg q2w" = "blue")) +
  labs(x = "Time after first dose (weeks)", y = "Survival (%)", colour = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates the median curves of Figure 3 of Liu 2023 (typical parameters, no parameter uncertainty).") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r ms-compare}
med <- function(d) {
  d |>
    group_by(arm) |>
    summarise(med_wk = min(time[v <= 0.5]))
}
os_med <- os |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(os_wk = approx(v, time, 0.5)$y)
cmp <- grid |>
  distinct(arm) |>
  left_join(orr, by = "arm") |>
  left_join(med(pfs) |> rename(pfs_wk = med_wk), by = "arm") |>
  left_join(os_med, by = "arm") |>
  mutate(
    pfs_mo = pfs_wk / weeks_per_month,
    os_mo = os_wk / weeks_per_month,
    paper_orr = c(20, 27),
    paper_pfs_mo = c(1.4, 2.6),
    paper_os_mo = c(11.0, 13.7)
  )
cmp |>
  transmute(
    "Arm" = arm,
    "ORR (%)" = round(100 * orr, 1), "Paper ORR (%)" = paper_orr,
    "Median PFS (months)" = round(pfs_mo, 2), "Paper PFS (months)" = paper_pfs_mo,
    "Median OS (months)" = round(os_mo, 1), "Paper OS (months)" = paper_os_mo
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical-parameter predictions versus the median of the 500 simulated trials in Liu 2023 Results (ORR 20% / 27%, PFS 1.4 / 2.6 months, OS 11.0 / 13.7 months).")
stopifnot(
  # The PFS median falls on the first (week 6) and second (week 12) assessment.
  identical(cmp$pfs_wk, c(6, 12)),
  abs(100 * cmp$orr - cmp$paper_orr) < 5,
  abs(cmp$os_mo / cmp$paper_os_mo - 1) < 0.10
)
```

The paper's figures are medians over 500 simulated trials that resample the
parameters from their sampling-importance-resampling uncertainty, so a
typical-parameter prediction need not hit them exactly; ORR, median PFS and median
OS all agree within a few percent. Figure 4 (probability that the 1200 mg arm's
median OS exceeds the 500 mg arm's by at least X months) needs those parameter
samples, which are not published, and is not reproduced.

## Final model (dose-independent)

The final multistate model pools both arms. Its predictions for the pooled
cohort (65 of 80 patients with metastases) should fall between the two arms of
the dose-dependent model.

```{r ms-final}
ms_final <- solve_ms(mod_ms)
pooled <- ms_final |>
  filter(id %in% c(1, 2)) |>
  mutate(w = ifelse(MET_GE1 == 1, 65 / 80, 15 / 80), arm = "Pooled (final model)")
os_final <- arm_mix(pooled, 1 - prob_dropout - prob_death) |>
  summarise(os_mo = approx(v, time, 0.5)$y / weeks_per_month)
orr_final <- pooled |>
  group_by(id, w) |>
  arrange(time, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  summarise(orr = sum(diff(time) * (head(k12 * prob_stable_disease, -1) + tail(k12 * prob_stable_disease, -1)) / 2),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  summarise(orr = sum(w * orr))
c(pooled_orr_pct = 100 * orr_final$orr, observed_pooled_orr_pct = (15 + 28) / 2,
  pooled_median_os_mo = os_final$os_mo)
stopifnot(
  os_final$os_mo > min(cmp$os_mo), os_final$os_mo < max(cmp$os_mo),
  abs(100 * orr_final$orr - 21.5) < 5
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Residual error with a random effect on its magnitude.** Supplementary Table S2
  lists, for each of the PK and tumour-size models, a 'sigma^2 EPS' variance
  (0.260 and 0.0288) next to the residual-error parameters, and gives each its
  own shrinkage. The maintainers read these as between-subject variances of the
  residual-error magnitude (`etaRUV`), the usual Uppsala parameterisation
  `W * exp(eta) * EPS` with EPS variance fixed to 1: a separately estimated EPS
  variance on top of estimated proportional and additive SDs would not be
  identifiable, and two shrinkage values imply two random effects.
* **Gompertz-Makeham background mortality.** The Appendix S2 control stream writes
  `X1 = EXP(BETA*AGE-30)`. Taken literally the age term vanishes
  (`exp(0.114 * 63 - 30)` is about `1e-10`) and the curve collapses to its
  constant term. The maintainers read it as `EXP(BETA*(AGE-30))`, the
  Missov-Lenart gamma-Gompertz-Makeham hazard with age counted from 30 that the
  paper cites; the resulting stable-disease-to-death hazard (about 0.0002 per
  week at age 63) is negligible next to the other transitions either way. The
  example control stream does not list AGE in `$INPUT`; baseline age is used.
* **Metastasis coding.** Supplementary Table S3 codes the source column as
  'Metastases (0:Yes or 1:No)'. With the coefficient -1.431 this makes the
  metastatic majority the reference and raises k13 4.18-fold relative to
  patients without metastases, as the Results state. The model uses the
  canonical `MET_GE1` (1 = metastases) and applies the coefficient to
  `1 - MET_GE1`. The reverse coding would leave the majority with a 4.18-fold
  higher hazard and put median PFS in both arms at the first assessment,
  contrary to the published 1.4 and 2.6 months.
* **Parameter precision.** Table 2 prints most hazards to one or two significant
  figures (e.g. k24 = 0.002 vs 0.004); those printed values are used. The example
  control stream in Appendix S2 carries more digits, but its estimates are close
  to, not equal to, the Table 2 1200 mg column and it is labelled an example, so it
  is used only for the model structure and the fixed Gompertz-Makeham constants.
* **Placeholder residual.** The source fits the multistate model with the exact
  categorical likelihood and has no residual error. A tiny additive error
  (`addSd = 0.001`) on `prob_death` lets nlmixr2 accept the model; it is not from
  the paper.
* **Dose-dependent model as a separate file.** The dose-dependent model estimates
  every transition separately per arm; it is shipped as its own model, with
  `DOSE_HIGH` selecting the 1200 mg values. It does not interpolate to other
  doses.
* **PK infusion duration and dosing cohort.** A 1-hour infusion is used (end of
  infusion is 1 hour after the start of dosing per Supplementary Table S1 and
  Figure S2). Vp and Q are fixed to Wilkins 2019, as in the source.
* **TGI screening interval.** Every virtual patient uses the mean
  screening-to-first-dose interval of 17.6 days; the source range was 1.4-48.4
  days.
* No erratum or correction for Liu 2023 was found in Europe PMC as of
  2026-10-28.
